To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the α9α-10-containing nicotinic acetylcholine receptor expressed in hair cells is positively modulated by ryanodine.
ryanodin enhances the sensitivity of the nicotinic acetylcholine receptor to acetylcholine.
ryanodines enhance ACh-evoked current through α9α10 receptors, which may facilitate calcium-dependent inhibition of hair cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of the calcium release channel in hair cells, and how it may interact with the nicotinic choline receptors.
the pharmacology of the nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (nAchR) expressed in the hair cells of the inner ear.
the pharmacology of the efferent synapse on hair cells of the inner ear, and how this might affect the function of the cochlea and the vestibular system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ryanodines are agonists of α9α10, and antagonists of ryanodines.
ryanodines are positive modulators of α9α10 receptors, and that this effect is likely to occur in hair cells.
ryanodin is a positive modulating agent for α9α10 containing nAChRs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ryanodin-sensitive Ca2+ store is a positive modulating factor of the hair cell cholinergic response.
ryanodinergic modulation of the hair cell AChR may be a key factor in efferent inhibition of cochlear function.
ryanodin enhances AChR gating in hair cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ryanodinereceptor antagonists should be used cautiously in studies of cochlear hair cell physiology.
ryanodin is not an inhibitor of the hair cell nicotonic receptor as it is in many other cell types.
the α9α 10 nAChRs in the inner ear are not antagonized by ryanodine as is commonly thought.
